name: China economy
summary: China's October output rose 4.8% and retail sales 0.4%, below forecasts; new home prices fell 2.4% a year
state: Statistics bureau data of 16 Nov showed October industrial output up 4.8% a year and retail sales up 0.4%, both below expectations, while fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% and property investment 21.6% in January–October (JKN). New home prices fell 0.1% on the month and 2.4% on the year, the slowest annual decline since November 2025 (Reuters). Searches on 18 Nov found no new developer default wave or financial contagion, so Normal holds with momentum weakening.
for_you: Weaker Chinese demand tends to weigh on exporters of commodities and goods to China. Households and firms elsewhere are not directly exposed to acute stress at present.
rubric_hit: Normal: growth near target (Q3 4.5%), no developer default wave or contagion; Watch would need deflation, defaults or growth clearly below target

sources.title: JKN — China's production and consumption slow down in October; investment contraction also deepens
Reuters (via 93.3 The Drive) — Drop in China's new home prices narrows to 11-month low

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
